title: Private upgrade orchestrator: zero-downtime migrations + LTS rollout gates
creator: Alex Chen
description: Build an orchestrated upgrade tooling suite for Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem) that supports zero-downtime schema and data-plane migrations, LTS/edge channels, progressive rollout gates (canary -> ramp -> full), and air-gapped upgrade flows. The tool should: (1) coordinate control-plane and data-plane component upgrades across heterogeneous customer environments; (2) run preflight and postflight checks; (3) perform reversible DB and KV-store migrations with compatibility shims; (4) expose safe rollback and emergency freeze; (5) integrate with Console rollouts and Dedicated autoscaler policies; and (6) generate audit logs for compliance. This ticket covers design, MVP implementation, test harness, runbooks, and initial customer pilot.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator CLI + agent can perform a staged upgrade (canary 5% -> ramp increments -> 100%) across a dedicated Private cluster without manual intervention
Preflight checks detect incompatible plugin versions, insufficient disk/CPU, and unimproved KMS config and fail upgrade with clear remediation steps
DB migrations run with online schema changes (pt-online-schema-change/gh-ost style) or dual-write compatibility layers and support non-blocking index builds
Automatic rollback path exists: if postflight health checks fail in canary, orchestrator aborts and rolls back canary nodes and leaves remaining nodes untouched
Audit trail created for each step: who triggered upgrade, commit SHAs, image digests, migration scripts run, and timing
Air-gapped upgrade artifacts (signed tarballs + verification manifest) support offline transfer and verification with checksums and GPG signatures
Integration tests demonstrate no more than 5% p99 latency regression during a canary upgrade in the staging harness
Runbook documentation and Support-run training session completed and recorded
tasks: Design orchestrator protocol (control-plane <-> agent RPC): idempotency, retries, backoff, and leader election
Define upgrade manifests: channel, version, image digests, migration steps, pre/post checks, gating policy
Implement agent (Go) for on-prem nodes: secure pull of artifacts, health reporting, dry-run mode, and local rollback
Build server-side orchestrator: plan generation, stage execution, parallelism controls, and safe concurrency limits
Create DB migration library: support safe ALTERs, backfill patterns, dual-write shim, and migration metadata table
Air-gap packaging flow: signer, artifact manifest, local verifier command to validate package and signatures
Console UI prototype for rollout visualization and manual overrides
Add observability hooks: step durations, failure reasons, tokenized traces, and per-node telemetry
End-to-end test harness: simulated clusters with mixed versions, network partitions, and KV corruption tests
Pilot with 2 customer private clusters and gather feedback
design_decisions: Adopt agent-based model rather than SSH-only: agents allow richer telemetry, idempotent RPCs, and offline buffering for intermittent connectivity
Use signed immutable artifacts (image digest + migration script checksum) for reproducibility and auditability
Favor asynchronous, eventual completion semantics for long-running migrations with polling and heartbeats instead of blocking RPCs
Implement gating policy DSL that composes health metrics (errors, p99, request success rate) and custom predicates for customer-specific checks
Support both online migration tools and built-in dual-write compatibility shims to accommodate customers without extended maintenance windows
tradeoffs: Agent model increases maintenance surface and requires secure key distribution, but reduces operational friction compared to per-upgrade SSH sessions
Dual-write compatibility adds code paths and temporary complexity but enables zero-downtime migrations for stateful store changes
Full rollback is best-effort for some migrations (e.g., destructive data transforms) — plan requires manual reconciliation steps documented in runbook
Air-gapped flow requires extra signing/inventory work and longer verification time, impacting PD for small patches

test_plan: Unit tests for agent RPCs and orchestration planner
Integration tests with staged network partitions to validate idempotency and retry behavior
Database migration integration tests with live replica and dual-write verification
Performance regression tests measuring p50/p95/p99 during canary upgrades
Security test: artifact signature verification, key rotation, TLS mutual auth, and supply-chain integrity checks
Pilot validation with two customer clusters, including an air-gapped cluster using signed tarballs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: migration causes data divergence. Mitigation: dual-write + read-compare tool and delayed cutover with traffic shadowing
Risk: agent compromise leads to supply-chain attack. Mitigation: artifact signatures + allowlist of image digests + periodic attestation
Risk: customers expect full rollback for destructive ops. Mitigation: explicit customer communication, export snapshots before applying destructive scripts
Risk: long-running migrations cause resource exhaustion. Mitigation: throttling, resource-guards and step-level timeouts
